title: Hyuck — Origin Story and Present-Day Fate (from Steve)
summary: Raw brainstorm from Steve (apparent creator/player of the gnoll Hyuck, already Blank Inheritance's canon Directorate founder) on how his character got here and what may have happened to him since — a god- and time-displaced wanderer possibly still alive now, 'contained' by the Directorate as a bioprison asset. No decisions made.
description:
Nothing in this entry is decided. Captured per Ingram's explicit instruction: 'No decisions made, just make notes of this conversation.'

Context this connects to, noticed while filing this idea rather than stated in the source conversation itself: Hyuck is not a new character proposal. He is already named in the bible as one of the Directorate's four founders, active roughly 200 years before Episode One alongside Anabala, Shucks Mordant, and Rupiah (ideas/story/blank-inheritance-master-timeline.md), and commemorated by the weathered/bronze gnoll statue in the harbour square (ideas/story/bible/locations/the-gnoll-statue.md, plaque reading 'Hyuck'). The bible's own Ledger (ideas/story/bible/LEDGER.md, entry #8) explicitly leaves open how the founders — other than the literally undead Shucks Mordant — have stayed active for two centuries. Steve appears to be the real-world originator/player of a gnoll PC named Hyuck from their own separate game, and this conversation is Ingram asking him directly how that character's history and fate should feed into Blank Inheritance's backstory. It reads as the missing link explaining why a gnoll founder exists in this worldbuilding at all, though that provenance is inferred, not stated outright in the log.

Opening prompt: Ingram asked how Hyuck would 'end up fitting into the adventure' long-term — whether Steve wanted him still alive several hundred years later, or to have left a legacy that lasted that long — explicitly framed as 'not a requirement,' just material toward 'a history which involves the first group.'

Character concept and origin, per Steve: Hyuck is 'a Gnollish version of Logan Nine-fingers' — spiritual without being religious, stumbling through his life's journey 'simply never quite falling down.' Anointed by a god named Yabadabba, he eventually falls foul of that god; before the resulting 'hammer of retribution' lands, he keeps tumbling into battles where he's hailed a hero, until he catastrophically offends everyone it's possible to offend. In response to Ingram asking whether the 'hero of legend' just isn't front-of-house presentable, the confirmed arrival mechanism emerged: messing with teleportation/time magic gets Hyuck ejected several hundred miles away and several hundred years into the future — landing him here, 'still an idiot.'

The skull/spirit thread: Hyuck carries his brother's skull, magically reincarnating 'memory by memory,' sharing Hyuck's body with him — 'the Jekyll to Hyuck's Hyde.' As a true ancestor-worshipper, Hyuck isn't threatened by this, even though (per Steve) it's actually a supernatural construct of Hyuck's own idealistic conception of his brother rather than the brother's genuine spirit. Steve called this body-sharing arrangement probably the most fun aspect of Hyuck as a character: 'It's all about belief - and idiots can believe absurd ideas.' Left hanging, unresolved: Steve floated that Hyuck may have been body-swapped along the way at some point, and might even be carrying a skull that isn't actually his brother's.

Core traits Steve flagged explicitly as load-bearing — 'those are the traits that should be retained - that's what makes Hyuck himself': too dim-witted to be argued out of his beliefs, too stubborn to change his mind, fiercely loyal to friends, fully committed in everything he does, an uncanny talent for offending literally everyone sooner or later, fast and violent when action is called for, and lucky in a pinch.

Present-day placement, brainstormed, nothing chosen: if Hyuck stays a gnoll, Steve figured he'd end up in 'the ultra-secret experimental program' — floated either as a mecha pilot with insanely sharp reflexes and extreme stamina plus heavy cybernetic enhancement, or as a source of genetic material to improve pilots' stamina (side effects raised as an explicit open question, never answered: 'But what would the side-effects be?!'). Ingram countered with a retired-pilot-turned-trainer angle. Given the campaign's own framing that the PCs make up roughly 90% of the available mecha pilots, Steve's next idea was that Hyuck would more plausibly be housed in a 'nightmarish bioprison,' exploited as a lab animal — which he judged Hyuck wouldn't mind much ('plenty of food and no gods to worry about'), unless he learned another party member or ally was being caged the same way, which 'wouldn't go so well.' Steve also noted that by this point in his life Hyuck is skilled enough at crafting that he could probably craft his way out of almost any containment. Ingram's refinement: the organisation running the mechs likely wouldn't imprison Hyuck directly — they'd keep him 'contained' simply by making sure he has what he needs while getting the most out of him possible. Ingram floated a further hook: Hyuck being brought out of containment during a genuine emergency, where his instability could cause more problems than it solves. Steve agreed, adding Hyuck is fairly passive if unprovoked, and it would take 'one hell of an emergency' before he makes a bad thing better.

Tie to the existing pilot-shortage pressure: Ingram connected this directly to the campaign's established reason the party (14-17-year-olds) are pressed into service so young — a lack of reliable pilots — as also being the pressure that could plausibly force the Directorate to risk bringing an unstable asset like Hyuck out of containment.

Mind-sharing / cockpit thread: Steve floated that because Hyuck is already used to moving his 'mind' around (per the body-swap/skull-sharing material above), interfacing with a Frame might be mentally less stressful for him than for other pilots — though he'd offend the Frame itself sooner or later regardless. Ingram connected this to 'some weird interplay between Hyuck, the skull and his arrangement with spirits' making the cockpit experience 'a psychic mess,' which she explicitly wants for story purposes: 'Loads of potential for things to go wrong. Which is what I need.'

Absurd-belief subplot options, brainstormed: Steve floated several directions for Hyuck's tendency to jump to absurd conclusions and get stuck there, once inside a Frame — that it's really a trapped deity he must help escape; that it's really his soulmate, rescuable by finding their skull; or simply a beloved pet, reincarnated. He also floated, then immediately discarded as unworkable, the Frame being a host for his brother's spirit — since that role is already filled by the skull. Ingram's favourite: Hyuck was told (by an unspecified someone) that he could make his brother 'big and strong again,' giving him a side-motivation to try to put his brother's soul into a Frame. Steve agreed this is a great way to lead Hyuck by the nose — right up until he actually figures out how to attempt it, which won't work, but will 'screw things up.' Ingram dubbed this 'Hyuck mad scientist mode.' Both agreed it fits the campaign's existing Evangelion-adjacent 'mirrors and shadows' register: regrets, undoing past mistakes, the interface between living flesh and machine, and the humanoid soul.
sourceContext: Pasted Discord conversation between Ingram and Steve, supplied directly 2026-09-16 with the explicit instruction 'No decisions made, just make notes of this conversation.' Original message timestamps in the source are relative ('Yesterday'); the exact date of the underlying conversation isn't given. The pasted log continues past this material into general GM-philosophy and tone comparison between Blank Inheritance and Steve's own PF2E campaign (referred to as 'BEL') — hero points that persist between sessions and can bend scenes, Directorate-issued starting gear, a preference for rarer/higher-stakes combat, and a shared lean toward fun-anime tone over grim dread. Not transcribed into this entry since it isn't Hyuck-specific and doesn't bear directly on this idea; flagged here so it isn't silently lost if it turns out to matter later.
openSubQuestions: Whether the 'several hundred miles and several hundred years' displacement is meant to land Hyuck at (or near) the Kortos incident / Directorate founding moment ~200 years before Episode One, or somewhere else on the timeline entirely.

Whether/where Hyuck is contained by the Directorate at Episode One's present, under what cover story, and whether that's the same graveyard as data/hangar/legacy-units.json (currently empty) or a separate facility entirely.
What side effects using Hyuck as a genetic-material source for pilot stamina/reflexes would carry — raised by Steve as a direct open question, never answered.

Whether the brother's-skull spirit and the 'put his brother's soul into a Frame' subplot are meant to intersect with the established Frame-core/pilot-seat lore (a Frame's core shapes itself into a seat for its pilot's true form) — flagged here as a strong thematic fit, not actually cross-checked against that lore in the source conversation. 2026-09-24 (LEDGER #32 item 7): only a Gen 2 Frame has a living core and a seat that shapes itself; Gen 1 Frames are Golarion technology with neither. So if this subplot happens, it is about a Gen 2 Frame.
The body-swap wrinkle Steve floated and left hanging: whether Hyuck might be carrying a skull that isn't really his brother's, or might himself not entirely be the Hyuck he believes himself to be.
resolvedSubQuestions: Whether present-day (Episode-One-era) Hyuck is meant to be the SAME individual as founder-Hyuck — contained/maintained by the Directorate continuously for ~200 years — which would double as a direct answer to the founders'-longevity question left open in ideas/story/bible/LEDGER.md entry #8. Not adopted; purely a connection noticed while filing this idea, not discussed in the source conversation. ANSWERED 2026-09-24 (LEDGER #28): yes, the same Hyuck, alive and on the base as the mad test pilot of the Directorate's worst Frame concepts. Not a contained asset; that framing is not adopted. How he has lived two centuries is still open (LEDGER #8).

Whether Hyuck ever appears as an active, interactable figure in play, remains statue-only background texture (per the-gnoll-statue.md's current 'unglossed civic furniture' tone rule), or both at different points on the timeline. ANSWERED 2026-09-24 (LEDGER #27, #28, #31): both. The statue stays civic furniture that a teacher is certain isn't Hyuck the founder (LEDGER #27); the living Hyuck is on the base and is revealed to the players slowly (LEDGER #28); and Steve plays him in flashbacks (LEDGER #31 item 12).
resolution:
PARTIAL, 2026-09-24 (Ingram, LEDGER #28): partly decided. Present-day Hyuck IS founder-Hyuck, alive and on the base -- "the mad test pilot of some of the Directorate's worst Frame concepts that never saw the light of day", revealed to the players slowly. This settles that he is alive and what he does; it does not adopt the rest of this pitch (the god, the time-magic mishap, the brother's skull, the contained-asset framing), which stays undecided. FURTHER, 2026-09-24 (LEDGER #31 item 12, Casebook D9): Steve plays Hyuck. He is one of the original group's players, and the four founders' players play them in flashbacks (Liam as Rupiah, Pippa as Anabala, Craig as Shucks, Steve as Hyuck). That settles this entry's inferred provenance: Hyuck was Steve's PC in Ingram's own original campaign, The Trouble with Mitflits (ideas/story/source-material/the-trouble-with-mitflits/), not a character from a separate game. (The old Foundry world lists Hyuck's player account as 'Thorn', presumably Steve's; unconfirmed.) The same ledger entry proposes, as Claude's fill-in, that the old 'berserk protocol' become Hyuck's emergency protocol for machines that fail under their pilots (open-questions.json#berserk-protocol-fate). No other part of the pitch is adopted: the god, the time-magic mishap, the brother's skull and the contained-asset framing all stay undecided. FURTHER, 2026-09-24 (LEDGER #32 item 11; Ingram, Casebook N8): "Hyuck absolutely would build something like that, but maybe we develop this idea to only happen with Gen 2. Leave it as an open question to be pinned down much later." So Hyuck's emergency protocol (the old 'berserk protocol', Mystery Ledger #8) would exist, but only with Gen 2 Frames -- Anabala's biomechanical machines built from actual mitflit technology, not the Golarion-built Gen 1 fleet (LEDGER #32 item 7). Its shape is open, to be pinned down much later (open-questions.json#berserk-protocol-fate).

DECIDED 2026-09-27 (Ingram, LEDGER #41): how he is alive. Gnolls join an older gnoll's spirit to a younger gnoll's body, a great honour with a risk: every transfer is a fight for the body. Hyuck has never lost one in two hundred years, and now shares his body with a multitude of other gnoll spirits, which is maddening. Claude named it the Carrying and gave it details (the skull between bodies, the bearer, the wrestle, riding and wearing), which fold in this pitch's brother's skull and 'well-looked-after asset' threads as proposals: ideas/story/bible/characters/hyuck.md. The god and the time-magic mishap are still not adopted.
